script: If you're going to steal the catalytics off my truck you should've checked if they were actually functional first, wasn't so funny when it was turn.. I started my truck at 2:45am and woke everyone up like a bad alarm clock—only to find my catalytic converters gone. The whole block smelled like burnt coffee and disappointment. I was like, "Yo, who just stole my cats?" but here's the thing… Those thieves were two kids from the neighborhood, driving a busted-up police Crown Victoria that looked like it was ready to explode. I didn't call the cops straight away; I called my buddy in code enforcement to keep it low key. He told the police I was planning a nuisance tow. What I didn't know was that the kids were probably the same ones who'd been hitting up the chicken shack all night. The Crown Vic was a nightmare—no plates, no insurance, no working taillights, and it rattled like a loose drum set from that trash sound system. They spent all day smoking at the chicken shack, living on the edge. I suspected catalytic theft was the motive, but until I saw the VIN I didn't have a clue who owned it. I spotted the car parked on a quiet street and called for a tow. The cops checked the VIN and discovered it hadn't been registered since 2011; the registered owner was someone else, no title, no paperwork. The police said we could tow it to the junkyard for a black title, because that's what you do with a ghost car. And that's when everything changed… The kids thought their car had been hijacked by a prankster, so they started roaming town, searching for their "stolen" vehicle. They found it at the junkyard and tried to snatch it back—one distracted the owner, the other tried to steal the car. The junkyard crew cut the driveshaft before they could get their hands on it. But here's the thing… They got arrested for trying to steal their own car back, and the junkyard used a crane to rip the car to shreds. I watched the frame fall apart like a toddler tearing apart a toy. The remains were a sad, twisted skeleton of a once proud vehicle. What I didn't know was how the cops would react to the chaos. They're out of jail now but haven't left their trailer, living in a loop of waiting and hoping. I did a drive‑by and spotted a beater Jeep Liberty in their driveway—no plates, no insurance, probably another piece of junk. I am already working with the cops to take that one too, because if I see it in public again, I won't miss the show next time. I am the only one who knows the full scoop, bestie, and honestly, the audacity of those kids is just… (I know, right?) The whole saga left my truck untouched, my neighborhood safe, and a story that's more epic than any TikTok drama. That's the tea, and that's the final word.
